split_rationale: 77x46 cannot hold 13 nodes and 15 relations at 100%. The split follows the source own seams: (v1) the physical OOB rail and what it reaches, (v2) the off-rack controller and its southbound API calls plus the NVSwitch tray software, (v3) the in-band compute software that runs on the hosts. Each view stays at 5-6 nodes, and no relation is drawn in two views.

source.md Relationship facts: the eleven audited relations (historical, unlabeled)
source.md Fixed constraints: exclusions, the OOB/API distinction, the one-OOB trunk, NVOS hosting NMX-C/T, no invented deploys/manages, host residency, uncertainty stays marked
abbreviations: "Redfish client" = nv-rms is a client on the OOB LAN and opens Redfish/HTTPS sessions
"Redfish power" = power-shelf controllers reached over Redfish/HTTPS
"power/serial" = the NVSwitch BMC OOB path is used for power and serial console only (no protocol named)
"NVUE/NMX gRPC" = NVUE REST plus NMX-C gRPC; SSH/SFTP omitted for width
"metrics :9400" = dcgm-exporter serves Prometheus metrics on port 9400 over the in-band network
"host-local" = both ends run on the compute host; the interface between them is not stated in the excerpts
"(mgmt)" / "(src build)" / "(tray)" / "(host)" = residency and licence markers, not part of the product name
uncertain_interface_qualifications: rms -> bmc_s: the source states the direct edge exists but names no protocol; the label records only what the source says that BMC path is used for (power/serial).

drvk -> fm: the excerpts never state an interface between the driver stack and Fabric Manager, so the edge is dashed and labelled "host-local" (the one thing the source does support: both run on the compute hosts). It is not drawn as a deploys/manages dependency.
oob -> nvos: historical and unlabeled, and it conflicts with the human correction; dropped rather than promoted to fact.
t2/t3 trunk spurs carry no label: the rail label on the corridor covers all three branches, and per-branch protocol text would promote guesses.
deliberate_drops: CDU controller and PDUs as OOB endpoints - not in the case node set, and the requested split is exactly three.
the OOB payload list beyond "power/serial" (fan/temperature telemetry, power draw, OS re-imaging) - no room, and it is a payload list, not an edge.
the OOB negative traffic claim ("no training, storage or NVLink traffic") - see known_defects d6.
SSH/SFTP from the NVSwitch southbound path - width.
Mission Control, UFM, NetQ, NGC, BCM, Slurm - excluded paid software / the source own exclusion.
Prometheus as a metrics consumer - not a node in the case node set.

known_defects.why_not_fixed: the source-build qualifier was added in v2 attempt 3, after the v1 budget was spent; the two markers are different facts (residency vs licence), not a contradiction, but the labels are not identical.

known_defects.defect: Extent is 76 of the 77 available columns, so the view fits with a single column of margin.

known_defects.defect: At frame 0 the dot glyph sits one cell past the first drawn cell of its arrow (v2 frame 0: dot at col 22 while the first drawn cell after the source port is col 21), although --check reports origins 4/4 and 2/2.

known_defects.defect: The "Redfish/HTTPS" label belongs to the trunk corridor (oob -> compute BMC) but reads as the rail protocol for all three branches.
known_defects.why_not_fixed: the trunk label is the only place the rail protocol can sit; the ownership is stated in the audit.

known_defects.defect: Two negative facts are not drawn in words: the OOB LAN carries no training/storage/NVLink traffic, and DCGM has nothing to do with OOB. The second is shown structurally (no OOB -> DCGM route exists anywhere); the first lives only in this file.
known_defects.why_not_fixed: no view has a free label slot, and inventing an "OOB (control only)" caption would add a claim the source does not phrase that way.

known_defects.defect: rms -> bmc_s is labelled "power/serial" although the source names no protocol for that hop.
known_defects.why_not_fixed: an unlabeled fourth API arrow would read as a protocol claim of the same weight as the other three; the label states the documented function and this file flags the gap.
